_provenance: HAND-AUTHORED source for the flagship-stack model. Edited by hand; the generated artifact book-models/flagship-stack.json is derived from this by book-models/flagship_stack_model.py. Add a stack = add a record here + its overview SVG + its appendix page, then `python3 book-models/flagship_stack_model.py regenerate`.
_note: A flagship stack is a PACKAGE of catalogue entries that together make one or more governed capabilities — the alternative-appendix deep-dives. Each record carries the stack's goal, the GEE capabilities it serves (a list of >= 1; most stacks serve one, some span two), an overview figure, and one entry per PART with the six fields the deep-dive template renders: role, failure, mechanism, seam (the interlock with adjacent parts), and durability. This file holds all seven finalized flagship stacks (reframe 260803).

stacks.name: The provenance + fidelity stack
stacks.goal: Reconstruct a remediated document's mutation history from the artifact itself, and catch any damage done through the sanctioned door — who and why for every change, and nothing silently lost.

parts.role: MARK — name every insertion so it is distinguishable from authored content and registry-covered by construction.
parts.failure: An inserted artifact is indistinguishable from what the author wrote, so nothing can tell what the tool added — and a validator cannot cover what it cannot name.
parts.mechanism: A three-way naming rule: an invisible insert takes a reserved prefix, a user-visible insert keeps an ordinary name, a spec-mandated name keeps its spec name — and every inserter records into one registry.
parts.seam: Opens the chain. It hands the next part a closed, registry-covered population of insertions to attribute; nothing enters the artifact unmarked, so the stamp-writer downstream has a complete set to stamp.
parts.durability: Durable and model-independent — a naming convention costs nothing at runtime and leans on no 2026 model capability. It fails only if an inserter bypasses the registry, which the fidelity gate then catches.

parts.role: EMIT — every sanctioned mutation embeds an attribution stamp, carrying its pass and its visibility, into the artifact itself.
parts.failure: A change is made but leaves no durable trace of who made it or why; once the file leaves the pipeline the mutation history is unrecoverable.
parts.mechanism: One sanctioned stamp-writer per format — the raw stamp mutation is ban-linted away — so every mutator verb writes its stamp through a single surface.
parts.seam: Takes the marked, registry-covered inserts from MARK and turns each sanctioned mutation into embedded evidence. It hands the wiring-lint a closed verb set to prove complete, and the changelog an embedded registry to read back.
parts.durability: Durable — evidence embedded in the artifact (not a side log) survives copy, download, and re-open. Cost is one stamp per mutation; it fails only where a mutation skips the sanctioned writer, which the next part forbids.

parts.role: COVER — a blocking lint asserts every mutator verb wires the stamp, so completeness is a guarantee, not an aspiration.
parts.failure: A new mutator lands without stamp wiring; provenance quietly develops a hole and 'we attribute every change' silently stops being true.
parts.mechanism: A build-time lint scans every mutator verb in the model Primitives and fails on any unwired one — the closed verb set held at zero open gaps.
parts.seam: Sits over EMIT. It reads the same closed verb set the stamp-writer serves and proves the writer is called across all of it, so the changelog READ downstream can trust the stamped population is complete.
parts.durability: Durable — a deterministic lint over a closed set does not decay. Its guarantee is only as strong as the one door it presumes: mutations must route through the sanctioned Primitives, held by a separate ban-lint.

parts.role: READ — a command reconstructs a human-legible ChangeLog from the embedded stamp registry, each entry a mutation attributed to its pass.
parts.failure: The provenance is present but unusable — stamps sit in the artifact with no consumer, so 'auditable' is a claim no one can exercise.
parts.mechanism: A command reads the embedded stamps and projects them into an attributed history — the mutation record reconstructed from the artifact itself, never a trusted external log.
parts.seam: Consumes what EMIT wrote and COVER proved complete. It turns the embedded evidence into the reconstructable history the stack's goal promises — provenance that finally has a reader.
parts.durability: Durable — a read-only projection of embedded data, with no runtime dependency; it reconstructs history from any conformant artifact and is exactly as complete as the stamps the wiring-lint guarantees.

parts.role: GATE — the fidelity gate: extract the input's content, assert input is a subset of output, and fail the job when meaning was dropped.
parts.failure: A remediation pass silently drops the user's content — the file looks fixed but lost a table, a note, a paragraph — and the damage ships invisibly.
parts.mechanism: A deterministic gate extracts input content and asserts it survives into the output, failing the job in production; a per-pass staging variant names which pass dropped it.
parts.seam: Closes the chain. Where MARK, EMIT, COVER, and READ attribute what the tool ADDED, the validator catches what a sanctioned pass silently REMOVED — damage done through the same door provenance covers. 'Content was lost somewhere' becomes 'pass N lost it.'
parts.durability: Durable and model-independent — a set-containment assertion over extracted content. Cost is one extract-and-compare per job; the per-pass variant is staging-only. It weakens only if extraction under-reads the format, bounded by the canonical reader.
